summary: Returns the value as an HtmlOutput, or throws.
description: An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard looks for the methods that define the type — `getContent`, `setTitle`, `setXFrameOptionsMode`. A stub that implements them passes, which is what makes code using this guard testable outside the runtime.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as an HtmlOutput.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is not an HtmlOutput.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript const output = HtmlService.createHtmlOutput("

hi

"); requireHtmlOutput(output); // => output requireHtmlOutput({}); // throws IllegalArgumentException requireHtmlOutput(null); // throws IllegalArgumentException ```
